subject: Swearing In of Police Chief John D. Buckley
overview: The City of Medford held a swearing-in ceremony to inaugurate John D. Buckley as the city's 11th permanent police chief. Following remarks by Mayor Stephanie Burke, Chief Buckley took the oath of office administered by Weston Police Chief Michael Goulding.

items.title: Welcome and Introductions
items.summary: Master of Ceremonies Mark Rumley opened the ceremony and introduced participating dignitaries and the family of Lieutenant John D. Buckley.

items.title: Presentation of Colors, Anthem, and Pledge
items.summary: The Medford Honor Guard posted the colors, Lillian Bates sang the national anthem, and Allison and Sarah Buckley led the Pledge of Allegiance.

items.title: Invocation
items.summary: Medford Police Department Chaplain Father Robert Casey delivered an invocation blessing the incoming chief and law enforcement personnel.

items.title: Address by Mayor Stephanie Burke
items.summary: Mayor Stephanie Burke outlined the department's history, praised retiring Chief Leo Sacco, and described incoming priorities including minority recruitment assistance and the construction of a new police headquarters.

items.title: Administration of Oath of Office
items.summary: Weston Police Chief Michael Goulding administered the oath of office to Chief John D. Buckley.

items.title: Remarks by Police Chief John D. Buckley
items.summary: Chief Buckley delivered an inaugural address pledging a guardian approach to policing, community engagement, departmental diversity, and gratitude to his mentors and family.

items.title: Acknowledgements
items.summary: Mark Rumley recognized attending regional police chiefs, city officials, municipal staff, and members of the City Council and School Committee.

items.title: Benediction
items.summary: Rabbi Bram David delivered the benediction, offering blessings for Chief Buckley, his family, and the community.

items.title: Closing and Retirement of Colors
items.summary: Mark Rumley invited attendees to a reception in the mayor's office as the Honor Guard retired the colors to conclude the ceremony.
